overlays.reason: Approved cumulative coordinator overlay. MOD-2 delegates parser, auth, routes, serialization, controllers, static responses and diagnostics; MOD-3.1 consumes coherent stream-key snapshots; MOD-5.2A/W1 moves classic request orchestration and security response ownership, W2 transfers template state and page chrome, W3 transfers server-list rendering and actions, W4 transfers transfer-list snapshot projection, W5 transfers fail-closed transfer actions, W6 transfers shared-file and search-result snapshot sorting, projection and rendering to bounded Unicode-safe modules, W7 freezes the complete Live API operation inventory, W8 transfers stream lifecycle, broadcast, HLS delivery, network status, channel and mesh response ownership to bounded portable controllers, W9 transfers network connection, traversal, keepalive and relay controls plus source-resolution diagnostics, privacy subscriptions, tunneled search and live diagnose/Kad directory responses to bounded portable controllers, W10 transfers NetLab/privacy settings, KRP/preflight/metrics/log/debug response ownership and the test-only loopback sabotage guard, W11 transfers the remaining compatibility pages, static-media delivery and privacy/Kad6 operations to a bounded portable controller while retaining the common authorization gate in the coordinator, W12 closes the WebServer facade with canonical controller headers, response-level referrer suppression, credential-safe rejection logging and removal of obsolete duplicate code, and the reviewed v9.2 reach-status adapter adds only the deny-listed read-only diagnostics route and cache refresh hook.

Approved cumulative interface overlay. Existing slices retain WebAuthPolicy and typed request metadata; W1 removes coordinator-owned gzip, W2 removes template and page-chrome ownership, W3 removes the legacy server row DTO and comparator, W4 removes transfer-list projection helpers, W6 removes the legacy shared-file row DTO and comparator after transferring stable snapshot projection and rendering to WebSharedFilesController, and W12 removes the final dead transfer comparator declarations and their unused SortParams helper.

MOD-3.1 delegates broadcaster and viewer lifecycle state, generation, retry timers, tunnel-session scalars and broadcaster secret lifetime to the two portable session modules; MOD-3.2 delegates ordered source/downstream membership, one canonical source cap, stable selection, atomic client replacement and IPv4 diversity while retaining locks, pointer lifetime, protocol projection and external I/O in the coordinator; MOD-3.3 delegates bounded chunk ingestion, serial ordering, expiration, availability and immutable lifetime to LiveChunkWindow; MOD-3.4 delegates session-scoped public-key pinning, post-storage verified replay windows, bounded durable trust records, pruning and trust transitions to LiveStreamSecurity; MOD-3.5 delegates stable child selection, bounded whole-batch reservations, backpressure admission and replacement-safe transport leases to LiveStreamFanout through a move-only transport adapter while retaining trust, metrics and orchestration; MOD-3.6 delegates bounded in-flight retry ownership, source replenishment and emergency lifecycle to LiveStreamRecovery while retaining trust mutation, peer lifetime, logging and packet transmission; MOD-3.7 delegates announce/Kad cadence, byte-compatible announce projection and immutable numerical diagnostics to LiveStreamAnnouncer and LiveStreamSnapshot while retaining the established manager lock and external snapshot acquisition order; MOD-5.2A/W12 adds the exact, immutable, bounded HLS read lease used by the closed WebServer facade.

MOD-3.1 replaces coordinator-owned broadcaster/viewer lifecycle scalars with explicit LiveBroadcastSession and LiveViewerSession composition; MOD-3.2 replaces the two coordinator-owned peer lists with a single portable LivePeerSet; MOD-3.3 replaces coordinator-owned viewer and broadcaster chunk containers with two bounded LiveChunkWindow instances and an explicit relay-sequence presence flag; MOD-3.4 replaces coordinator-owned pin, replay and trust stores with bounded LiveStreamSecurity composition plus a pointer-free legacy trust adapter; MOD-3.5 composes bounded LiveStreamFanout state while Packet and CUpDownClient remain behind the transport adapter; MOD-3.6 replaces coordinator-owned in-flight, replenishment and emergency fields with bounded LiveStreamRecovery composition plus a typed endpoint adapter; MOD-3.7 replaces coordinator-owned announce/Kad timers with LiveStreamAnnouncer composition and moves public pointer-free diagnostic types to LiveStreamSnapshot, reducing the header below the 700-line hard stop; MOD-5.2A/W12 exposes the manager-owned HLS read-lease contract without moving manager locking or filesystem authority into the web layer.
